name: Data lineage LPG (PROV-inspired)
description: Labeled property graph ontology for data lineage, inspired by the W3C PROV-O vocabulary. It is not a PROV-O serialization and does not promise a round trip to RDF: references to PROV terms point to the closest concept, not to an equivalence. Logical objects (Dataset, Column, Job) are stable over time; versions (DatasetVersion, ColumnVersion, JobVersion) are immutable and carry the lineage, so questions can be asked as of a point in time. Run-level facts (USED, WAS_GENERATED_BY) record what a run read and wrote. They do not mean that every output depends on every input. Asserted derivations (WAS_DERIVED_FROM, COLUMN_DERIVED_FROM) come from a named source such as OpenLineage column lineage, a SQL parser or a dbt manifest. Potential dependencies computed from run inputs and outputs are stored separately as DEPENDS_ON. Time: generatedAt is when a version was produced, publishedAt when it was exposed to consumers, validFrom and validTo when it is the version consumers should see. Point-in-time queries use validFrom and validTo, not generatedAt alone. Invalidation never deletes history. Cross-level consistency rules described on relationships, such as a column version belonging to a version of the column's own dataset, are enforced by ingestion; the format cannot express them. KEY and existence constraints require Neo4j Enterprise Edition or Aura.

entity.label: Entity
entity.description: Base label for everything that has lineage: datasets, columns, jobs and their versions. Abstract by convention (not a field of the format): every Entity node also carries a more specific label. Holds the id uniqueness constraint shared by all subtypes.

id.description: Stable identifier, unique across all entities.
id.name: id

activity.label: Activity
activity.description: Base label for things that happen over time and read or write entities. Abstract by convention: every Activity node also carries a more specific label, such as Run.

id.description: Stable identifier, unique across all activities.
id.name: id

agent.label: Agent
agent.description: Base label for people, software and organizations that are responsible for runs or own assets. Abstract by convention: every Agent node also carries a more specific label.

id.description: Stable identifier, unique across all agents.
id.name: id

dataset.description: The logical asset, stable over time: a table, topic, file, model or dashboard. Identified by namespace and name, as in OpenLineage. Lineage attaches to its versions, not to it directly.

id.description: Stable identifier, for example ds:snowflake://acme/stg.orders. Existence and uniqueness are enforced by the id constraints on the base label (Entity, Activity or Agent), which every node of this kind must carry explicitly.
id.name: id

namespace.description: Namespace of the data source, for example snowflake://acme or postgres://db1:5432. Required: covered by the KEY constraint on namespace and name.
namespace.name: namespace

name.description: Name of the dataset within its namespace, for example stg.orders. Required: covered by the KEY constraint on namespace and name.
name.name: name

system.description: System that hosts the dataset, for example snowflake.
system.name: system

retiredAt.description: When the dataset was logically retired. Retirement does not delete its versions or lineage.
retiredAt.name: retiredAt

dataset-version.description: An immutable snapshot of a dataset, produced by at most one run. Runs use and generate dataset versions, which is what makes point-in-time lineage possible. Source versions that no tracked run produced have no generation.

id.description: Stable identifier, for example dsv:snowflake://acme/stg.orders@17. Existence and uniqueness are enforced by the id constraints on the base label (Entity, Activity or Agent), which every node of this kind must carry explicitly.
id.name: id

version.description: Version as reported by the source system: a number, snapshot id, commit id or hash. Opaque; do not order versions by this value.
version.name: version

generatedAt.description: When the producing run finished writing this version.
generatedAt.name: generatedAt

publishedAt.description: When this version was exposed to consumers. Absent if it was never published or if publication is not tracked.
publishedAt.name: publishedAt

validFrom.description: Start of the period in which this is the version consumers should see. Set by ingestion; it may differ from generatedAt, for example for backfills or delayed publication.
validFrom.name: validFrom

validTo.description: End of that period, exclusive. Absent while the version is current.
validTo.name: validTo

invalidatedAt.description: When this version was declared invalid, for example after a backfill or a deletion request. The version and its lineage are kept.
invalidatedAt.name: invalidatedAt

schemaHash.description: Hash of the schema of this version.
schemaHash.name: schemaHash

column.description: A logical column of a dataset, stable across versions. Its versions carry the column-level lineage.

id.description: Stable identifier, for example col:snowflake://acme/stg.orders.price. Existence and uniqueness are enforced by the id constraints on the base label (Entity, Activity or Agent), which every node of this kind must carry explicitly.
id.name: id

column-version.description: A column as it exists in one dataset version: name and type at that point in time. Column-level lineage connects column versions, so an assertion always belongs to the run that produced the dataset version.

id.description: Stable identifier, for example colv:snowflake://acme/stg.orders@17.price. Existence and uniqueness are enforced by the id constraints on the base label (Entity, Activity or Agent), which every node of this kind must carry explicitly.
id.name: id

name.description: Column name in this dataset version.
name.name: name

dataType.description: Data type as reported by the source system, for example NUMBER(10,2).
dataType.name: dataType

ordinal.description: Position of the column in the dataset version.
ordinal.name: ordinal

nullable.description: Whether the column accepts null values in this version.
nullable.name: nullable

job.description: The logical job, stable over time: a dbt model, Airflow task or Spark job. Identified by namespace and name, as in OpenLineage.

id.description: Stable identifier, for example job:airflow://prod/stg_orders. Existence and uniqueness are enforced by the id constraints on the base label (Entity, Activity or Agent), which every node of this kind must carry explicitly.
id.name: id

namespace.description: Namespace of the scheduler or project, for example airflow://prod. Required: covered by the KEY constraint on namespace and name.
namespace.name: namespace

name.description: Name of the job within its namespace. Required: covered by the KEY constraint on namespace and name.
name.name: name

job-version.description: An immutable definition of a job: code plus the dependencies and configuration that change what it does. Execution parameters belong to the run, not here. Plays the role of a PROV plan.

id.description: Stable identifier, for example jobv:airflow://prod/stg_orders@git:ab12. Existence and uniqueness are enforced by the id constraints on the base label (Entity, Activity or Agent), which every node of this kind must carry explicitly.
id.name: id

definitionHash.description: Hash of the effective definition, such as compiled SQL plus pinned dependencies and configuration. Two runs with the same hash ran the same definition.
definitionHash.name: definitionHash

artifactRef.description: Reference to the built artifact, for example a container image digest or a dbt manifest.
artifactRef.name: artifactRef

configRef.description: Reference to the configuration version that is part of the definition.
configRef.name: configRef

run.description: One execution of a job. Uses input dataset versions and generates output dataset versions. Ingestion folds all events of a run into this node and never moves it from a terminal status back to RUNNING.

id.description: Stable identifier, for example run:<OpenLineage runId>. Existence and uniqueness are enforced by the Activity id constraints; the node must carry the Activity label explicitly.
id.name: id

endedAt.description: When the run reached a terminal status.
endedAt.name: endedAt

status.description: Normalized status, not an OpenLineage event type. RUNNING: not finished. SUCCESS: finished and all outputs valid. FAILED or ABORTED: finished without valid outputs. PARTIAL: finished with an error, but some outputs were committed and are valid; which ones is recorded on each generated dataset version through validFrom and invalidatedAt. SUCCESS, FAILED, ABORTED and PARTIAL are terminal.
status.name: status

lastEventType.description: Type of the latest event applied, as sent by OpenLineage.
lastEventType.name: lastEventType

lastEventTime.description: eventTime of the latest event applied. Ingestion ignores events older than this value and events that would leave a terminal status.
lastEventTime.name: lastEventTime

observedAt.description: When ingestion last updated this run.
observedAt.name: observedAt

parameters.description: Effective execution parameters as sanitized JSON, for example the logical date or partition. Never store secrets; use parametersRef for sensitive values.
parameters.name: parameters

parametersRef.description: Reference to the full parameters in a secure store.
parametersRef.name: parametersRef

person.description: A person responsible for an asset or a run, such as an owner or steward.

id.description: Stable identifier, for example agent:alice. Existence and uniqueness are enforced by the Agent id constraints; the node must carry the Agent label explicitly.
id.name: id

software-agent.description: A piece of software that executes runs, such as an orchestrator or BI server.

id.description: Stable identifier, for example agent:dbt. Existence and uniqueness are enforced by the Agent id constraints; the node must carry the Agent label explicitly.
id.name: id

organization.description: A team or organization on whose behalf agents act.

id.description: Stable identifier, for example agent:data-platform. Existence and uniqueness are enforced by the Agent id constraints; the node must carry the Agent label explicitly.
id.name: id

used.description: A run read a dataset version. A run-level fact: it does not say which outputs depend on it.

role.description: Role of the input in the run, for example input or lookup.
role.name: role

was-generated-by.description: A dataset version was written by a run. Each version has at most one generation; source versions have none.

role.description: Role of the output in the run, for example output.
role.name: role

depends-on.description: Potential dependency between dataset versions, computed from a run's inputs and outputs (every output of the run to every input). An over-approximation used to speed up traversals, not a proven derivation. Rebuild it from USED and WAS_GENERATED_BY; never edit it by hand.

runId.description: Id of the run the dependency was computed from.
runId.name: runId

was-derived-from.description: Asserted dataset-level derivation: a named source states that the derived version was computed from the source version. Unlike DEPENDS_ON, it is evidence.

runId.description: Id of the run that generated the target-side version. Context for filtering, not a referential integrity guarantee: ingestion must check that this run generated the dataset version of the derived side.
runId.name: runId

jobVersionId.description: Id of the job version of that run.
jobVersionId.name: jobVersionId

evidenceRef.description: Reference to the evidence, for example an event id, a manifest path or a parsed query hash.
evidenceRef.name: evidenceRef

transformationType.description: Kind of dependency, as in the OpenLineage column lineage facet. DIRECT: the value is computed from the source. INDIRECT: the source affects the result, for example through a filter, join or grouping.
transformationType.name: transformationType

transformationSubtype.description: Finer kind, for example IDENTITY, TRANSFORMATION, AGGREGATION, FILTER or JOIN.
transformationSubtype.name: transformationSubtype

expression.description: Transformation applied, for example price * qty. Descriptive only.
expression.name: expression

column-derived-from.description: Asserted column-level derivation between column versions. The derived column version belongs to a dataset version generated by the run in runId, so assertions from different runs or job versions never mix. The source column version must belong to a dataset version that run used.

runId.description: Id of the run that generated the target-side version. Context for filtering, not a referential integrity guarantee: ingestion must check that this run generated the dataset version of the derived side.
runId.name: runId

jobVersionId.description: Id of the job version of that run.
jobVersionId.name: jobVersionId

evidenceRef.description: Reference to the evidence, for example an event id, a manifest path or a parsed query hash.
evidenceRef.name: evidenceRef

transformationType.description: Kind of dependency, as in the OpenLineage column lineage facet. DIRECT: the value is computed from the source. INDIRECT: the source affects the result, for example through a filter, join or grouping.
transformationType.name: transformationType

transformationSubtype.description: Finer kind, for example IDENTITY, TRANSFORMATION, AGGREGATION, FILTER or JOIN.
transformationSubtype.name: transformationSubtype

expression.description: Transformation applied, for example price * qty. Descriptive only.
expression.name: expression

version-of-dataset.description: A dataset version is a snapshot of exactly one logical dataset.

has-column.description: A logical dataset has a logical column. Each column belongs to exactly one dataset.

has-column-version.description: A dataset version contains a column version. Each column version belongs to exactly one dataset version.

version-of-column.description: A column version is a version of exactly one logical column. Ingestion must ensure that the column belongs to the dataset of the column version's dataset version.

version-of-job.description: A job version is a definition of exactly one logical job.

run-of.description: A run executes exactly one logical job. Always known from the event, even when the code version is not.

had-plan.description: The job version a run executed, when known. An LPG shortcut: in PROV-O the plan is attached to the association between an activity and an agent, not to the activity. Ingestion must ensure that the job version is a version of the run's job.

was-informed-by.description: A run used something that another run generated, or was triggered by it.

was-associated-with.description: An agent was responsible for a run.

role.description: Role of the agent in the run, for example executor or triggeredBy.
role.name: role

was-attributed-to.description: An entity is attributed to an agent, for example a dataset to its owner or steward.

role.description: Role of the agent for the entity, for example owner or steward.
role.name: role

acted-on-behalf-of.description: An agent acted on behalf of another agent, for example an orchestrator on behalf of a team.

was-invalidated-by.description: A dataset version became invalid because of a run, for example a backfill or a deletion job. Set together with invalidatedAt; the version and its lineage are kept.

reason.description: Why the version was invalidated, for example backfill or deletion request.
reason.name: reason
